dedupe_keys.name: us coastex observation based probabilistic reanalysis of storm surge and sea level extremes for the united states

description: US-CoastEX: Observation-based probabilistic reanalysis of storm surge and sea level extremes for the United States is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Joao Morim et al. Reliable estimates of storm surge and sea level extremes with proper uncertainty quantification are key for cost-effective risk/adaptation planning. However, observational estimates are often unavailable or uncertain along most coastlines owing to data scarcity. Here, we provide a fully observational-driven probabilistic dataset (US-CoastEX) of storm surge and sea level extremes for the U.S. coast (1950–2020). Coverage: national (US); published in 2025. Formats: NetCDF. The data are held in Zenodo and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
